locations.quote: I will attach a recertifcation interval to each resource, which its descendants inherit, and open a campaign whenever the interval elapses. The maintainer decides to keep or revoke each grant, and the platform stores every decision as an immutable record. Ignored campaigns escalate and may revoke grants automatically, but never in a campaign that reached nobody. The platform logs every change with the person who made it, and the admin event log of Keycloak keeps a second copy.

locations.quote: Requesters do not know who manages which resource. A student who needs a host, a channel, and a repository asks several people and meanwhile borrows the session of a colleague or works under a shared account.

Access outlives its purpose and leaves no trace. No grant carries an expiry date, so access piles up and former students keep SSH access months after they leave, the same decay that Schaad et al. [SMJ01] and Kern et al. [Ker+02] report from industry.
